new_claims.statement: There is no universal lower bound on |sigma| ||H n|| from the three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis plus a unit aggregate two-row wedge, even in a strict-N3 diffuse family. The explicit A_k has Delta(H)=1, |sigma| ||Hn||=k^-2, max physical coefficient=k^-1, max physical 2x2 principal determinant<=k^-2, and at least three eigenvalues of modulus>=1.

For an orthonormal two-frame U with leverages ell_i and Pluecker weights w_ij, the disjoint-basis mass satisfies rho=1-sum ell_i^2+sum w_ij^2. Therefore rho<rho0 forces a physical row with leverage >(1-rho0)/2. Combined with the completed two-hub theorem, large rho gives a core-independent O(interval length) density bound while small rho yields literal physical localization.

For A_k=k^-1 e1e1^T+k(e1 a^T+a e1^T)+k^-1(e2 b^T+b e2^T)+c c^T with three disjoint flat size-k^4 banks, every admissible cap-one product law has continuous output density bounded by (5/3)e^(3/5)(1-k^-4)^(-3/5)<3.157.

partner_result_applied.application: Applied with r=1, lambda=1, W=[c,k a,k^-1 b], det(W^TW)=1 and exact rho=(1-k^-4)^3, giving ||p_Q||inf<3.157 and P(Q in L)<3.157|L| for the new strict-N3 diffuse family.
